author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read SailPoint Identity Security Cloud audit events from the Search API events index. The example bridge in bridges/sailpoint-isc-events pulls them and posts them to HTTP Ingest. Sign-ins and sign-outs, MFA checks, personal access token use, SSO app launches and password changes go to Auth, and every other event goes to CloudAudit.
notes:
Setup:
- SailPoint Identity Security Cloud has no syslog or push stream for its audit events, so these parsers read events pulled from the Search API events index by the example bridge in bridges/sailpoint-isc-events and posted to HTTP Ingest.
- The bridge puts "sailpoint_record": "event" in front of each event.

Field mapping:
- Sign-ins and sign-outs (the AUTHENTICATION, SAML2 and SESSION actions), MFA checks, personal access token use, SSO app launches and password changes go to Auth, by the action names in SailPoint's Audit Events Reference.
- Every other event, API client and identity provider changes of type AUTH included, goes to CloudAudit, with technicalName as the event name and SailPoint's type as the event type.
- SailPoint documents ipAddress as the address of the target system, so it goes to target_address in Auth and to additional_event_data in CloudAudit.
- The attributes object differs by event and SailPoint doesn't document every key, so it is kept as JSON.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the documented EventDocument shape, with action names from the Audit Events Reference.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-15 (138 of 138 fields matched the emulator, in 3 runs), and each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent.
- No built-in parser in that tenant claimed these events in 3 Run Tests.
